info.what: Flags skipped sequential levels (e.g., jumping from H1 directly to H3) or fake structural classes imitating headings. Note: Starting a page directly with an H2 is not flagged as a skipped level.
info.why: Headings map the document's structure. Skipping levels breaks the outline and deeply confuses screen reader navigation. WCAG 1.3.1: Info and Relationships
info.fix: Ensure headings increment by only one level at a time (e.g., an H2 should only be followed by an H2 or H3). Use proper native heading tags (<h1> - <h6>) instead of styling generic <div> elements to look like headings.

info.what: Flags form controls missing a linked <label for>, an aria-label, or a direct <label> wrapper.
info.why: Screen readers cannot announce what the input is for. The user will focus the field and only hear 'Edit text', with no context. WCAG 3.3.2: Labels or Instructions
info.fix: Add a <label for="input-id"> that targets the input's ID, nest the input directly inside a <label>, or provide a descriptive aria-label.

info.what: Flags inputs relying solely on the placeholder attribute for their accessible name.
info.why: Placeholders disappear when a user begins typing, removing the instructions. Furthermore, default placeholder colors frequently fail text contrast minimums. WCAG 4.1.2: Name, Role, Value
info.fix: Provide a persistent, programmatic label (like a <label for="id"> or aria-label) instead of relying solely on the placeholder.

info.what: Flags interactive elements where the visible text is completely overridden by an aria-label that does not include the visible text.
info.why: Voice dictation users rely on visible text. If they say 'Click Buy' but the ARIA label is 'Add to cart', the voice command will fail. WCAG 2.5.3: Label in Name
info.fix: Ensure the aria-label value begins with or clearly includes the exact visible text displayed on the element.

info.what: Computes the exact width and height pixel boundaries of interactive elements, color-coding thresholds.
info.why: Undersized targets prevent users with fine motor impairments (like hand tremors) from activating controls accurately without accidental clicks. WCAG 2.5.8: Target Size (Minimum) WCAG 2.5.5: Target Size(Enhanced)
info.fix: Use CSS padding or explicit width/height declarations to expand the clickable footprint of the element to meet minimum thresholds (24x24px for AA, 44x44px for AAA).

info.what: Traces the sequential path of focusable elements and flags traps. Main page elements are numbered sequentially (#1, #2). When focus enters an iframe, elements are marked with an [Iframe] tag and a hierarchical decimal (e.g., #4.1 indicates the 1st focusable element inside the 4th tab stop). Nested iframes add further decimals (e.g., [Nested] #4.2.1).
info.why: Simulates the exact path of the TAB key. Ensures logical flow and visualizes deeply nested cross-frame boundaries. WCAG 2.4.3: Focus Order
info.fix: Review the drawn path line for logical sequential flow (left-to-right, top-to-bottom). Verify that elements flagged as 'Focusable in Aria-Hidden' are safely deactivated (using inert or tabindex="-1")when their parent layer is closed.

info.what: Computes the final accessible name by simulating the browser's fallback calculation sequence: aria-labelledby, then aria-label, then native linked labels or inner text, and finally the title attribute.
info.why: Reveals exactly what a screen reader will announce. Identifies mismatching accessible names and dangerously silent controls. WCAG 4.1.2: Name, Role, Value
info.fix: Review the visually printed text. Ensure active controls missing a name (red flags) are properly labeled using visible text or an aria-label.
